title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Premium Revision Paper #2

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #2
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does removing waste mean for a plant? (1 mark)
   A. Cutting its own leaves
   B. Getting rid of things its body does not need
   C. Sending out roots
   D. Throwing away its seeds

2. Which of these is a plant that has a thick main root with thin side roots? (1 mark)
   A. Grass
   B. Bean plant
   C. Maize
   D. Wheat

3. A student puts a plant in a box with a small hole on one side. After a week, the plant bends toward the hole. This shows that plants (1 mark)
   A. need no water
   B. make sound
   C. respond to light
   D. walk

4. Which sign of life do ALL living things eventually show? (1 mark)
   A. Flying
   B. Making seeds
   C. Dying
   D. Flowering

5. What is an invertebrate? (1 mark)
   A. An animal with hair
   B. An animal without a backbone
   C. An animal with a backbone
   D. An animal that flies

6. Which of these is a vertebrate? (1 mark)
   A. Snail
   B. Hen
   C. Spider
   D. Ant

7. Which animal group breathes using gills? (1 mark)
   A. Birds
   B. Fish
   C. Mammals
   D. Reptiles

8. What is a vertebrate? (1 mark)
   A. An animal with a backbone
   B. An animal with six legs
   C. An animal that lives in water only
   D. An animal without bones

9. What do vertebrates have inside their bodies that invertebrates do not? (1 mark)
   A. Feathers
   B. Six legs
   C. A shell
   D. A backbone

10. Which of these is a good use of a school deworming day? (1 mark)
   A. Give them to animals
   B. Take the tablets when given by the health worker
   C. Refuse to take them
   D. Throw them away

11. What is vomiting? (1 mark)
   A. Passing loose faeces
   B. Chewing food
   C. Food coming out through the mouth
   D. Feeling hungry

12. What is bloating? (1 mark)
   A. A cut in the mouth
   B. Tiredness
   C. A full, swollen tummy often with gas
   D. Loose faeces

13. Which of these is a way of storing leftover food safely? (1 mark)
   A. Sharing it with flies
   B. Leaving it uncovered in the sun
   C. Putting it on the floor
   D. Covering it and keeping it clean

14. What are the symptoms of worms mentioned in the lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Loud voice
   B. Fast running
   C. Seeing worms in faeces, itchy anus, weakness
   D. Clear skin

15. Which of these helps to keep teeth healthy? (1 mark)
   A. Eating many sweets
   B. Never visiting a dentist
   C. Brushing twice a day
   D. Biting hard objects

16. What is saliva? (1 mark)
   A. A type of waste
   B. A liquid in the mouth that wets food
   C. A germ
   D. A tube in the stomach

17. Why should you chew your food well? (1 mark)
   A. It makes food smaller for easier digestion
   B. It makes food colder
   C. It stops you drinking water
   D. It makes food heavier

18. Which of these is a correct grouping? (1 mark)
   A. Milk, water and juice are liquids
   B. Steam, oil and rice are gases
   C. Chalk, water and steam are solids
   D. Air, stone and salt are gases

19. Which of these is matter? (1 mark)
   A. Light
   B. Heat
   C. Sound
   D. Water

20. Which waste is both decomposable and from an animal? (1 mark)
   A. Dung
   B. Plastic
   C. Glass
   D. Tin

21. What is solid waste? (1 mark)
   A. Air from a tyre
   B. Smoke from a fire
   C. Dirty water
   D. Unwanted solid material that is thrown away

22. Why should waste bins have lids? (1 mark)
   A. To make them look nice
   B. To make waste rot faster
   C. To make waste heavier
   D. To keep out flies and rats

23. Which of these is non-decomposable waste? (1 mark)
   A. Banana peel
   B. Tin can
   C. Egg shells
   D. Leaves

24. What does recycle mean? (1 mark)
   A. Make waste into new things
   B. Bury waste
   C. Throw waste away
   D. Burn waste

25. Which of these is true of water? (1 mark)
   A. Animals do not need water
   B. Only humans need water
   C. Water is needed by all living things
   D. Plants do not need water

26. Which reused water is safe for drinking? (1 mark)
   A. Water that washed vegetables
   B. None of the used washing water
   C. Water that washed a car
   D. Water that washed clothes

27. A jerrycan holds 20 litres. A leaking tap wastes 40 litres in a day. How many jerrycans is that? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 60
   C. 20
   D. 4

28. Which of these uses less water to wash a car? (1 mark)
   A. A running hose
   B. A bucket and sponge
   C. A large drum poured everywhere
   D. A long shower

29. Why do we need water for farming? (1 mark)
   A. To make stones
   B. To bake bricks only
   C. Crops and livestock need water
   D. To make wind

30. A cyclist pedals harder and goes faster. What effect of force is this? (1 mark)
   A. Decreases speed
   B. Changes shape
   C. Increases speed
   D. Stops motion

31. How can a farmer keep a wheelbarrow running smoothly? (1 mark)
   A. Add sand to the wheel
   B. Oil its moving joints
   C. Leave it in the rain
   D. Use rough paint

32. What direction does friction act in compared with the motion of an object? (1 mark)
   A. Sideways only
   B. Upwards only
   C. The same
   D. Opposite

33. Which force is at work when you pour water and it flows down a slope? (1 mark)
   A. Light
   B. Gravity
   C. Sound
   D. Magnetism only

34. Which surface gives the most friction? (1 mark)
   A. An oiled floor
   B. A polished tile
   C. A rough carpet
   D. A smooth ice surface

35. When light hits an opaque object, what forms behind it? (1 mark)
   A. Sound
   B. A rainbow
   C. A shadow
   D. A flame

36. Which of these can be a cheap way of lighting a house in a rural area? (1 mark)
   A. Many electric heaters
   B. Solar lamp
   C. Hundreds of candles
   D. A big generator

37. Which of these should be kept away from fire? (1 mark)
   A. Clean water
   B. Paraffin and petrol
   C. Salt
   D. Stones

38. Why should pupils not touch hot sufurias? (1 mark)
   A. They become cold
   B. They make sound
   C. They become bigger
   D. They can burn their skin

39. Which of these is a fuel? (1 mark)
   A. Firewood
   B. Sand
   C. Glass
   D. Clean water

40. What is the source of heat that dries fish in the sun? (1 mark)
   A. Electricity
   B. The sun
   C. A jiko
   D. A torch

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain the difference between transparent, translucent and opaque materials. (3 marks)

42. A bat has wings. Explain why it is not a bird. (3 marks)

43. Describe how a pupil can tell that an earthworm is an animal. (3 marks)

44. Draw a simple diagram of the digestive system and label mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine and anus. (5 marks)

45. Name two invertebrates that are found near your school. (2 marks)

46. Explain how farmers use light to discourage pests and animals. (4 marks)

47. Give two natural and two artificial sources of light. (2 marks)

48. Describe the characteristics that show that animals are living things. Use examples. (5 marks)

49. A school tap leaks 2 litres every hour. How much water is lost in a school day of 8 hours and in 5 school days? (3 marks)

50. Describe an experiment to show that a solid keeps its shape but a liquid takes the shape of its container. State what you would observe. (5 marks)

51. Name the parts of the digestive system in the order food passes through them. (2 marks)

52. Explain why light is important in our daily lives. (5 marks)

53. What is evaporation? Give one example. (2 marks)

54. Explain why deworming is important and state two other ways of preventing worms. (4 marks)

55. Name two things a farmer can do to save water. (2 marks)

56. Explain why rubbing your hands makes them warm. (2 marks)

57. Name four safety measures to observe in a kitchen and give a reason for each. (4 marks)

58. Give two ways in which water is wasted at school. (2 marks)

59. Convert 4 kg into grams. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #2 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Getting rid of things its body does not need
   Living things must remove waste made in their bodies.

2. B — Bean plant
   A bean plant has a main root with side roots. Maize and grass have many thin roots.

3. C — respond to light
   The plant responds to the light entering through the hole.

4. C — Dying
   Every living thing dies one day, but not all fly, flower or make seeds.

5. B — An animal without a backbone
   Invertebrates have no backbone.

6. B — Hen
   A hen is a bird and has a backbone.

7. B — Fish
   Fish take oxygen from water with gills.

8. A — An animal with a backbone
   Vertebrates have a backbone.

9. D — A backbone
   A backbone is the feature that defines vertebrates.

10. B — Take the tablets when given by the health worker
   Follow the health worker's advice.

11. C — Food coming out through the mouth
   Vomiting is throwing up food through the mouth.

12. C — A full, swollen tummy often with gas
   Bloating means the tummy feels full and swollen.

13. D — Covering it and keeping it clean
   Covered food is safer from germs.

14. C — Seeing worms in faeces, itchy anus, weakness
   These are signs that worms may be present.

15. C — Brushing twice a day
   Brushing removes food remains and prevents tooth decay.

16. B — A liquid in the mouth that wets food
   Saliva wets food and starts to digest starchy foods.

17. A — It makes food smaller for easier digestion
   Chewing breaks food into small pieces.

18. A — Milk, water and juice are liquids
   Milk, water and juice are all liquids.

19. D — Water
   Water has mass and takes up space. Light, sound and heat are not matter.

20. A — Dung
   Animal dung rots and can be used as manure.

21. D — Unwanted solid material that is thrown away
   Solid waste is unwanted solid material.

22. D — To keep out flies and rats
   Covered bins reduce smell and pests.

23. B — Tin can
   Metal does not rot easily.

24. A — Make waste into new things
   Recycling makes new things from old materials.

25. C — Water is needed by all living things
   All living things need water.

26. B — None of the used washing water
   Used washing water is not safe to drink.

27. A — 2
   40 divided by 20 = 2.

28. B — A bucket and sponge
   A bucket limits the water used.

29. C — Crops and livestock need water
   Water is needed for plants and animals.

30. C — Increases speed
   More force increases speed.

31. B — Oil its moving joints
   Oil reduces friction.

32. D — Opposite
   Friction acts against motion.

33. B — Gravity
   Gravity pulls water downhill.

34. C — A rough carpet
   Rough surfaces give more friction.

35. C — A shadow
   Blocked light makes a shadow.

36. B — Solar lamp
   Solar lamps use free energy from the sun.

37. B — Paraffin and petrol
   Fuels can burn or explode.

38. D — They can burn their skin
   Hot metal burns.

39. A — Firewood
   Fuels burn to give heat.

40. B — The sun
   Sun heat dries fish.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Transparent materials let almost all light through. Translucent materials let some light through. Opaque materials do not let light through.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: A bat has fur and feeds its young on milk. Birds have feathers and lay eggs. So a bat is a mammal.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fur, 1 mark for milk, 1 mark for mammal.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: It feeds on soil, grows, breathes, moves, responds to touch, reproduces and removes waste. It shows the signs of life.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sign, up to 3.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: A neat tube drawn from mouth to anus with each part labelled in the correct order.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the drawing and 1 mark for each of four correct labels.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any two correct examples such as ant, earthworm, snail, butterfly, spider.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct invertebrate.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: They use bright or flashing lights at night near fields or animal pens to scare wild animals away. Lamps near sheds help to see thieves or pests.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for bright lights, 1 mark for scaring away animals and 2 marks for examples.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Natural: sun, stars, lightning, firefly. Artificial: bulb, torch, candle, lantern, solar lamp.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two correct natural and 1 mark for two correct artificial.

48. (5 marks)
   Answer: Animals feed, grow, breathe, reproduce, remove waste, move, respond and die. Give examples such as a goat eating grass and a hen laying eggs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sign to a maximum of 5.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: 16 litres in one day and 80 litres in five days.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 2 x 8, 1 mark for 16, 1 mark for 16 x 5 = 80.

50. (5 marks)
   Answer: Use a stone and water. Put the stone in a cup and then in a bowl. It keeps its shape. Pour water in the cup and then into the bowl and its shape changes with the container. Conclusion: solids keep shape but liquids take the container's shape.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for materials, 1 mark for stone in both containers, 1 mark for water in both, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for conclusion.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum, anus.
   Working / marking points: Award 2 marks for the correct order. 1 mark if at most two parts are out of order.

52. (5 marks)
   Answer: It lets us see, keeps us safe, helps plants to make food, dries clothes, gives solar power and discourages pests.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point up to 5.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: Liquid water turning into water vapour, for example wet clothes drying.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for an example.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: Worms live in the intestines and take food and make us weak. Deworming kills them. Wear shoes, wash hands, keep nails short.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons and 1 mark each for other ways.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: Use drip irrigation, use mulch, water at cooler times, harvest rainwater.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: Rubbing causes friction and friction produces heat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for friction and 1 mark for heat.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Handles inwards to avoid knocking pots, gloves to avoid burns, children away to avoid accidents, switch off iron to avoid fire.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each with reason.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Leaving taps running, leaking taps or pipes, using too much water for washing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: 4000 g.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 4 x 1000 and 1 mark for the answer with units.
